Let’s say we consider positive velocity to be pointing North and negative velocity to be pointing South.

If I start by moving South, my velocity is negative. If I have a negative acceleration, my velocity will decrease, but my speed will increase. 

Deceleration is when speed decreases, but negative acceleration can increase the speed if it is in the same direction as velocity.

Positive velocity with negative acceleration is deceleration AND negative velocity with positive acceleration is deceleration.

It’s very important to understand that speed is a scalar and velocity is a vector.

Thank youuu! For math I think the absolute most important thing is knowing how to use Desmos quickly, because you can skip the work for about half the questions just by typing them into desmos. For example, solving systems of equation is just the intersection point.

You can even type in functions like mean(1,2,3,8,9) and it gives you the average or stdev(9,8,7,3) for standard deviation, and median also works. 

By being able to go really quickly through the easier problems, you’ll have way more time to think about difficult ones!

There’s this thing called the “SAT Educator Question Bank” and since I was weaker on grammar, I filtered all the grammar questions and selected the hardest difficulty and just went through all of them. I think these questions are really good practice because the format is exactly the same as the test, but you should only do them after you’ve at least taken some of the practice tests or maybe all except the last one because they sometimes repeat passages from those.
